# TypeScript

PocketOne strips the types from `.ts` and `.tsx` files and runs them; it never checks them. To check them, use `tsc` or your editor with the types PocketOne writes for your app.

When the app starts, `pb_data/types.d.ts` gets the declarations of the whole JS API, PocketPages included. PocketPages adds no globals: its types live in the `pages` namespace and you use them by name.

## Set up

Put a `tsconfig.json` next to `pb_pages`:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022", "module": "ESNext", "moduleResolution": "Bundler", "lib": ["ES2022"],
    "strict": true, "noEmit": true, "allowImportingTsExtensions": true, "skipLibCheck": true,
    "jsx": "preserve"
  },
  "include": ["pb_data/types.d.ts", "pb_pages/**/*"]
}
```

Start the app once so `pb_data/types.d.ts` exists, then run `npx tsc -p .` or open the folder in your editor. `"jsx": "preserve"` lets `tsc` check JSX without a React runtime; `skipLibCheck` skips two type errors inside PocketBase's own generated declarations.

## The types

| Type | For |
|---|---|
| `pages.Context` | `ctx`: `req`, `res`, `data`, `params`, `route`, `auth`, `app` and the helpers |
| `pages.Handlers` | A `+page.ts` or `+api.ts`: `load`, `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete` |
| `pages.Middleware` | A `+middleware.ts`: `(ctx, next) => ...` |
| `pages.Config` | `+config.ts` |
| `pages.PluginFactory`, `pages.Plugin` | A JS plugin |
| `pages.Props<L>` | A `.tsx` page, layout or partial; `L` types an `include`'s locals |

`satisfies` keeps your own return types and checks the shape:

```ts
// pb_pages/products/[id]/+page.ts
export default {
  async load(ctx) {
    ctx.data.product = await ctx.app.findRecordById.async('products', ctx.params.id)
  },
  post(ctx) {
    const { qty } = ctx.req.body<{ qty: number }>()
    return ctx.res.redirect(`/products/${ctx.params.id}`, { flash: `Added ${qty}` })
  },
} satisfies pages.Handlers
```

```ts
// pb_pages/admin/+middleware.ts
const admin: pages.Middleware = (ctx, next) => {
  if (!ctx.auth) return ctx.res.redirect('/login')
  return next()
}
export default admin
```

```tsx
// pb_pages/_private/badge.tsx, rendered with ctx.include('badge', { label: 'new' })
export default function Badge({ label, asset }: pages.Props<{ label: string }>) {
  return <span class="badge"><img src={asset('star.svg')} />{label}</span>
}
```

A component you import and use as `<Card />` gets only the props you pass it, not `ctx` or `asset`, so give it a props type of its own.

## Your own data, plugins and helpers

`ctx.data` accepts any key. To type yours, or what a JS plugin adds to `ctx`, add to the interfaces in a `.d.ts` file of your own, say `pb_pages/types.d.ts`:

```ts
declare namespace pages {
  interface Data {
    product?: core.Record
    section?: string
  }
  interface Context {
    hello(): string // added by your plugin's extendContext
  }
}
```

`ctx.session` and `ctx.realtime` are typed as always there; at runtime they exist only when the `auth` and `realtime` plugins are on in `+config.js`.
